text:
maria_chen: Hey, ran into a weird one after installing redwoodctl via Homebrew on my MBP (Monterey). Auth flow returns success in browser but local 'redwoodctl local serve' keeps prompting for login in a loop.
kevin: ugh. did you upgrade from older CLI or is this a fresh install?
maria_chen: Fresh install. Brew says redwoodctl 0.9.2. I grabbed the device-code login flow: `redwoodctl auth login --device-code` — browser shows success, token saved? but `redwoodctl whoami` returns unauthenticated.
jamal: can you paste `ls -l $(which redwoodctl)` and `cat ~/.config/redwoodctl/config` (sanitized) ? sometimes perms or symlink target got messed by SIP.
maria_chen: sure
maria_chen: ```
$ which redwoodctl
/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
$ ls -l /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
lrwxr-xr-x  1 root  admin  48 Feb 23 12:01 /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl -> ../Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.2/bin/redwoodctl
```
maria_chen: config dir exists at `~/.config/redwoodctl` and has `profiles.json` but token fields look empty.
kevin: interesting. SIP shouldn't affect /usr/local, but if the installer ran `--user` vs system or Homebrew migrated, there can be mismatch between binary user and config dir owner. What are perms on `~/.config/redwoodctl`?
maria_chen: `drwxr-x---  3 maria  staff  96 Feb 23 12:02 ~/.config/redwoodctl`
jamal: that looks fine. Do you have `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG` or `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set? if the CLI expects XDG and your shell has a different env in non-interactive contexts, the daemon/local serve might run without the env and look in /etc or fallback path.
maria_chen: nope, nothing set. zsh login vs non-login shell difference maybe?
kevin: also check the credential helper path. On mac we use a small keyring helper binary at `/usr/local/opt/redwoodctl/credential-helper` (example). If the symlink points to a keg-only location, subprocess can't exec under `local serve` sandbox.
maria_chen: ran `ps aux | grep redwoodctl` while reproducing, saw `redwoodctl local serve` spawn a helper with ENOENT. logs: ```
2026-02-10T18:41:12Z ERROR helper: exec /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.2/libexec/cred-helper: no such file or directory
```
jamal: bingo. brew cellars sometimes put helper into `libexec` and the packaged config expects a relative path. On some macs the postinstall script moves helpers and the symlink resolves differently when SIP relocated /usr/local during upgrade.
kevin: quick workaround: create a tiny shim script at the expected path that proxies to the new helper location, or set REDWOODCTL_CRED_HELPER env to point to the actual binary.
maria_chen: easy enough. found helper at `/usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.2/bin/cred-helper`. created shim: `mkdir -p /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.2/libexec && ln -s ../bin/cred-helper /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.2/libexec/cred-helper` and restarted `redwoodctl local serve`. auth flow now completes and `redwoodctl whoami` shows my user.
kevin: awesome. we should add a postinstall check in the Homebrew formula to ensure libexec links or update the packaged config to prefer env override.
jamal: raising a tiny PR to homebrew formula and adding fallback in CLI: try configured helper path, then try sibling bin/libexec locations, then fallback to env. also add clear error message: "credential helper not found: set REDWOODCTL_CRED_HELPER or reinstall".
maria_chen: SGTM. one more note: for anyone hitting login loops, `REDWOODCTL_LOG=debug redwoodctl local serve` shows the helper exec error pretty clearly. saved me a lot of head scratching. :+1:
install-bot: Homebrew postinstall note: if you see credential helper issues after upgrade, run `brew postinstall redwoodctl` or `brew link --overwrite redwoodctl` to restore expected symlinks.
kevin: adding this to the devex troubleshooting doc under "macOS installer quirks". thanks for the reproduction and fix writeup, maria.
maria_chen: happy to file the issue and the local fix notes. will ping when PR is up.
